version.author: Giorgio Robino
version.changelog: Initial public ALPHA: stereo Peak/RMS envelope history with optional MIDI note references and an explicit loop companion.

version.author: Giorgio Robino
version.changelog: 0.8.0 The package moved from MIDI/ccscope to ccscope, so ReaPack installs it in Effects/ccscope and sees a different package: remove the old one after updating, and re-add the effect to projects that used it. Also a shorter description, no sliders mentioned (hidden since 0.7.0), and the roadmap left to the issues and discussions. 0.7.8 CC ramps draw as straight diagonals instead of an artificial staircase; genuine peaks, troughs and clipped boundaries remain. 0.7.7 Nothing visible changed: one conductor plus five library files, so a change touches one file. Update through ReaPack. 0.7.6 History spans the whole chosen time window at any event rate, and changing WIN keeps what was retained. Spikes stay as an envelope. Limits and validation: GitHub issue #5. 0.7.5 Less work per frame, same picture: cheaper redraws on busy sessions. Capacity and GUI refresh rate unchanged. GitHub issue #23. 0.7.4 The control bar spans the plot, flush left and right, with cut corners; the engaged button turns amber. Narrow windows put the two buttons after the selectors. 0.7.3 The bar sits on the window's own black, aligned with the plot's left edge: one vertical line through the whole plugin. 0.7.2 The three metrics are fixed columns with right-aligned numbers, so a changing value no longer shifts what follows it. 0.7.1 No change in behaviour: a packaging fix, 0.7.0 shipped with the previous release notes. 0.7.0 The plugin draws its own control bar, seven cells in place of the slider strip, which cost 190 px of window height. Automation, presets and the Param button keep working. 0.6.5 The "now" edge of the graph is a single line: no tick on the frame. 0.6.4 The pair list can sit beside the plot, roughly doubling the pairs a short, wide window shows; too narrow a window falls back and says so. 0.6.3 A taller window shows more pairs, not only a taller graph; the status line says how many are on screen. 0.6.2 Channel filter, combining with the CC filter: graph, bars and the "showing N of M" line read the same filtered list. 0.6.1 Packaging fix: 0.6.0 could not load. Use 0.6.1 or newer. 0.6.0 Renamed to CCScope (was "MIDI CC Visualizer"): uninstall the old package. One colour per (CC, channel), labelled time axis, Freeze and Clear, DOTS as a choice, and metrics corrected: exactly one second, 500 events/s per pair, jitter that ignores gaps. 0.5.2 Correctness pass, no new features: CC values from 10 upwards no longer overwrote each other's data, one filter for graph and bars, and jitter measured on the audio-sample clock. 0.5.1 Cleaner bar layout: explicit Events/Rate/Jitter labels. 0.5 Multi-channel support: CC data, colours and metrics tracked per (CC, channel).

version.author: Giorgio Robino
version.changelog: 0.12.2 The ReaPack changelog shows this release only. The block had kept the whole history since 0.5, and ReaPack displays what it finds there for every version: previous entries are preserved by reapack-index on its own, so the block holds the current version. No change in the plugin.

version.author: Giorgio Robino
version.changelog: Add readable hover help for row identity, values and metrics (#18). Rename Timing to Jitter without +/-; calculations unchanged. Left-align metric fields.

version.author: Giorgio Robino
version.changelog: Add six selectable color palettes with stable CC colors across channels. Show all channel choices when space permits, with scrolling in shorter windows.

version.author: Giorgio Robino
version.changelog: **One marker per bucket, not two.** A bucket's two endpoints sat 1-2 px apart at a 10 s window, so the dots read as pairs instead of as a rhythm; the line still passes through both, and a bucket holding one event keeps its marker.

version.author: Giorgio Robino
version.changelog: - **Every event, not ten a second.** The trace was drawn from a 10 Hz bucket aggregate, so "every event" could place at most ten markers a second while the controller sent a hundred: the ring now holds every event and a mark is drawn per event, decimated and declared only past the measured drawing budget.

version.author: Giorgio Robino
version.changelog: **The trace is a step, not a ramp.** A CC message sets a value and the controller holds it; joining two events with a diagonal drew the values in between, which were never on the wire. The trace now holds the previous value horizontally and jumps vertically, as REAPER's own CC lanes do. **Every event is a mark.** Marks are no longer thinned: what adapts to a dense stream is the mark itself, a circle while the events are apart and a short tick when they would fuse into a band. **The held value continues, dashed.** After the last event the value is still held, so three modes replace the old ones: points, points with the step, points with the step and the dashed tail to now. **A filter now hides what it says.** With a CC or channel filter on, the graph drew events of the pairs it was hiding and stopped short of the newest visible ones: the pair-to-slot map was never initialised, and the drawing loop was bounded by the number of visible events instead of by the window.

version.author: Giorgio Robino
version.changelog: **The tail survives the window.** When the last event scrolls out of it the value is still held, so the dashed coda is drawn from the left edge at that value instead of the plot going blank.

version.author: Giorgio Robino
version.changelog: **The bar track is drawn in both layouts.** Below the plot a short bar was a stub on nothing while the same row beside the plot sat on a grey track showing the 0-127 range: the two layouts now show the same row the same way.

version.author: Giorgio Robino
version.changelog: **The silence before a burst is kept.** When a CC resumed after a gap, its first new event erased the dashed hold it was interrupting; the trace now starts from the value the event before the window was holding, so the gap stays visible.

version.author: Giorgio Robino
version.changelog: **Colours and names are yours, in a file you edit.** `ccscope_cc_table.jsfx-inc` lists every CC with a colour and a short name; the six palettes and the COLOR cell are gone, and the parameter that drove them stays declared so existing presets keep their numbering. **A shade can no longer disappear.** The channels of one CC are four shades of its colour, drawn by moving luminance instead of multiplying the red, green and blue channels, which used to bury a blue in the background. **The status line names the stream** instead of counting it when there is exactly one: `CC11 expr` rather than `1 stream`.

version.author: Giorgio Robino
version.changelog: **Keep event points in every DOTS mode.** Dense streams retain circle markers instead of vertical ticks; points-only mode draws no connecting lines, and step and tail geometry is unchanged. [#27](https://github.com/solyarisoftware/reaper/issues/27)

version.author: Giorgio Robino
version.changelog: **The third column now describes delivery timing instead of guessing at quality.** Timing shows raw p50/p95 message intervals in ms with the interval count n: coincident timestamps and long pauses both stay, so a burst-and-pause stream is visible instead of being summarised as steady. Resting on it adds min/max, the coincident-timestamp percentage and a secondary gap-filtered jitter, labelled as filtered. Quality words and the old single jitter number are gone; Messages and Motion are unchanged. [#30](https://github.com/solyarisoftware/reaper/discussions/30)

version.author: Giorgio Robino
version.changelog: 0.1.0 -- First release. Rate in notes per second, Humanize, Balance, Ramp Up / Ramp Down / Ramp Depth, drone and two parallel trills, transport-stop flush.
